lots.title: Provision of Cleaning Services - Corporate Buildings & Public facilities in Parks & Open Spaces
lots.description: Output-based cleaning and hygiene service for the London Borough of Bexley covering corporate buildings (civic/administrative offices, libraries, community hubs, customer service areas, operational depots, Danson House) and parks & open spaces assets (public conveniences, changing rooms, pavilions, visitor/education centres, function rooms and immediately adjacent external approaches). The Contractor provides comprehensive cleaning, consumables, mobile provision, NFC/QR proof of service, biohazard response and environmental/social-value commitments from contract commencement in September 2026. Areas must meet defined outcomes at required times, with method and resourcing selected by the Contractor.
requirements: Deliver output-based cleaning meeting acceptable standards across hard floors, soft floors, vertical/horizontal surfaces, sanitary ware and glazing; areas must be safe, dry and fit for use at the start of the defined operating day.
Prevent cross-contamination using recognised colour-coding; toilet/shower equipment must never be used elsewhere.
Operate a visual quality measurement regime with sampling and scoring; Council and Contractor agree audit forms, sampling plans and scoring during mobilisation.
Use environmentally preferable products; bleach is prohibited. Maintain Safety Data Sheets and COSHH risk assessments on site; lockable chemical storage required.

Corporate buildings frequencies: daily touch-point sanitisation, waste removal, vacuum/mop floors, desk wipe, kitchens/tea points, toilets/washrooms full clean and restock, receptions, lifts, consumable replenishment; weekly internal glass/partitions, high/low dusting, edge/skirting detail; monthly/quarterly floor burnish, carpet spot and extraction, blinds clean, high-level dust.

Public conveniences frequencies: minimum 4 cleans per day per block in summer (Apr-Sep) and 2 per day per block in winter (Oct-Mar), scheduled to include opening and closing bands; quarterly deep cleans as standard; biannual heavy deep clean where specified; ad-hoc mobile response between cleans.

Changing rooms & pavilions: in-season clean after each booked session or minimum twice weekly (showers, benches, floors, drains, touchpoints); off-season weekly routine and monthly deep bathroom descaling.
Function/Visitor rooms in parks: clean after each event/booking with interim top-ups between back-to-back bookings; monthly internal glazing and quarterly floor care.

External approaches (where in scope): daily litter pick, spot wash/spot mop thresholds, sanitisation of hand-contact points; summer monthly / winter quarterly jet-wash or steam-clean of approaches and gullies; quarterly gum removal in high-use sites.

Reactive & emergency cleaning via Helpdesk-routed requests for spills, biohazards, floods, toilet incidents, glass breakages and litter hotspots. Biohazard response: make safe within 30 minutes and complete sanitisation within 2 hours; provide barriers, signage and immediate Council notification where facilities are taken out of action.

Keyholding, access control and alarm management: securely hold, log, track and store all keys, access cards and alarm codes; open and secure premises at agreed times; set and unset intruder alarms in accordance with Council procedures; report any activations, faults or issues immediately; no key copying or code sharing without explicit written authorisation.

Provide a dedicated vehicle-based mobile cleaning team to deliver public convenience rounds, event uplifts, absence cover and daytime reactivity across parks, equipped with water-saving/low-moisture equipment, biohazard kits and signage; mobile deployment included in the Fixed Price Service Fee.

Contractor supplies, maintains in safe condition and keeps adequately stocked all equipment and consumables (including toilet tissue, hand towels/hand-dryers, soap, bin liners, sanitary waste liners).

Manage waste streams: general/recyclable to site bins, sanitary/nappy on schedule with duty-of-care documentation, sharps/clinical in UN-approved containers with compliant removal and consignment/transfer notes, and reactive hazardous/special removals fully compliant with legislation.

Comply with all relevant H&S legislation and Council policies; provide RAMS for all tasks (including working at height, jet-washing, confined access, sharps, biohazards); provide role-appropriate BICSc-aligned training and infection-control modules; toilets/parks teams trained in sharps and biohazard handling; staff hold DBS clearance where required.

Environmental and social-value commitments: use biodegradable/low-toxicity products and refill systems where practicable; minimise single-use plastics; deploy electric or ultra-low-emission vehicles for mobile rounds where reasonably practicable; conserve water via low-moisture methods and grey water for external cleaning where feasible; quarterly reporting on chemical SKU count, plastics reduction, vehicle CO2e and water saving; support local employment, pay the London Living Wage (or as directed) and offer apprenticeships/training.

Monitoring: NFC/QR checkpoints with time-stamped logs at public toilets and remote sites; upload geo-tagged photos for deep cleans and remedials; monthly site self-audits, monthly joint audits across a sample, and ad-hoc Council audits; maintain on-site communication books where requested.

Reporting: monthly operational pack (attendance, NFC logs, audit scores, complaints/compliments, incidents/accidents, consumables usage, sustainability metrics, additional works) and quarterly performance report (trends, KPI summary, improvement plan updates, innovation proposals).

Pricing structure: Fixed Price Service Fee covers routine baselines per site including mobile rounds, standard consumables and agreed deep cleans; Variable Works priced by PSQM/item/hour for external fabric cleaning, escalated jet-washing/gum removal, specialist floor finishes, blinds/curtains, comms/IT rooms (dry methods), post-event cleans beyond baseline, out-of-hours labour above baseline, hazardous/special waste uplifts and specialist medical-standard cleans.

Mobilisation deliverables prior to service start: site surveys; risk assessments; method statements; equipment and chemical lists; staffing and supervision plan; NFC point plans; quality audit templates; and initial Site-Specific Cleaning Frequency Tables.
TUPE (where applicable) managed under prevailing regulations; provide a workforce transition plan and ensure service continuity from Day 1.

warnings.message: The tender specification does not cite any CPV codes for Lot 6. The parent notice carries building-services CPV codes (50700000-2, 50750000-7, 71315000-9) which are not specific to cleaning services; a cleaning-specific code such as 90910000-9 is plausible but not evidenced in this document, so the lot's cpv_codes array has been left empty.
KPI table in Section 12.2 leaves the 'Quality score' target cell blank and the 'Customer satisfaction' remedy cell blank; those values have been reproduced verbatim rather than inferred.
Source document_extraction row reports page_count=0 (DOCX source rendered as a single logical page). Evidence anchors therefore reference section headings rather than numeric page numbers.

Document is the Draft Specification for Lot 6 only (Cleaning Services). Sibling lots 1-5 and 7-11 exist on the parent Building Services Framework notice but are out of scope for this specification document and are not emitted here.
